actually **closer to the current Yaffle deployment model than TFC remote runs are**.\n\nWhy:\n\n- CLI operations will often target **multiple workspaces**\n- they should respect the **workspace DAG**\n- they should show up in the **same environment-oriented UI**\n- they should reuse **run-group fairness and orchestration**\n\nThat means a Yaffle CLI invocation likely maps naturally to:\n\n- `run_group` with `trigger = \"manual\"`\n- `workspace_deployments` for the selected workspaces\n- normalized execution requests underneath those deployments\n\nIn contrast, TFC/OpenTofu remote execution remains a **single-workspace run protocol** and still needs its own workspace-run resources.\n\n### Consequence\n\nThis suggests two parallel product surfaces over one shared execution core:\n\n#### Yaffle-native orchestration surface\n\nInputs:\n\n- GitHub webhooks\n- Yaffle UI actions\n- `yaffle` CLI\n\nProduct objects:\n\n- `run_group`\n- `workspace_deployment`\n- approvals\n- DAG visualization\n\n#### Compatibility surface\n\nInputs:\n\n- OpenTofu/TFC-style cloud backend API\n\nProduct objects:\n\n- `configuration_version`\n- `tfc_run`\n- `tfc_plan`\n- `tfc_apply`\n\nBoth should feed the same remote execution substrate.\n\n## Proposed CLI command model\n\n### Core commands\n\n#### `yaffle ls`\n\nPreview which workspaces a selector resolves to.\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle ls --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n```\n\n#### `yaffle plan`\n\nCreate a remote plan run for the selected workspaces.\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n#### `yaffle apply`\n\nApply a previously reviewed plan or trigger apply for selected workspaces subject to policy.\n\n```bash\nyaffle apply --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\nyaffle apply --from-run rg_123\n```\n\n#### `yaffle destroy`\n\nDestroy selected workspaces, respecting reverse-DAG ordering.\n\n```bash\nyaffle destroy --pr 123 --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n#### `yaffle logs`\n\nStream logs for a run group, deployment, or run.\n\n```bash\nyaffle logs run_123\nyaffle logs deploy_123\n```\n\n#### `yaffle graph`\n\nShow the resolved DAG for the current target + selector.\n\n```bash\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\n### Common targeting flags\n\nRecommended shared flags:\n\n- `--select`, `-s`\n- `--exclude`\n- `--env <name>`\n- `--pr <number>`\n- `--ref <git-ref>` later\n- `--wait`\n- `--json`\n- `--output <fmt>` where it improves UX\n\n### Safety defaults\n\nRecommended defaults:\n\n- `plan` is allowed broadly\n- `apply` requires explicit target context (`--env` or `--pr`)\n- protected environments still require approval/policy checks\n- all CLI execution is remote by default\n- all CLI execution is audited and surfaced in UI as `source = cli`\n\n## Source material model\n\n### CLI should upload source, not assume a webhook event\n\nA strong first-party CLI should be able to run against:\n\n- current git HEAD\n- optionally uncommitted local changes\n\nThat implies a source upload model similar to TFC configuration uploads, but at **repo scope** rather than single-workspace scope.\n\n### Recommended primitive\n\nIntroduce a generalized source bundle concept later, even if the MVP stores this in existing fields first.\n\nPossible shape:\n\n- `scope = repo | workspace`\n- `origin = webhook_scan | cli_upload | tfc_upload`\n- archive key / size / checksum\n- repo metadata if available\n- head SHA if available\n- dirty flag for local uncommitted uploads\n\nPotential mapping:\n\n- webhook flow: scanner-produced repo bundle\n- CLI flow: client-uploaded repo bundle\n- TFC flow: uploaded workspace bundle\n\nThis bundle concept can unify artifact handling over time.\n\n## Selector syntax proposal\n\nTake strong inspiration from dbt's DAG selector syntax.\n\n### Principles\n\n- terse enough for daily use\n- composable without becoming unreadable\n- graph-aware by default\n- easy to preview with `yaffle ls`\n- safe to store and display in UI/audit logs\n\n### MVP selector model\n\n#### Default selector\n\nA bare selector matches workspace path.\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\nEquivalent to:\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"path:apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n#### Graph operators\n\nBorrow dbt-style operators:\n\n- `foo` = just this workspace\n- `+foo` = workspace and all upstream dependencies\n- `foo+` = workspace and all downstream dependents\n- `+foo+` = both upstream and downstream\n- `2+foo+1` = quantified expansion depth\n- `@foo` = workspace, downstream dependents, and whatever upstream dependencies are needed to make those dependents runnable\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"apps/web/infra+\"\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"2+apps/infra\"\n```\n\n### Why `@` is useful in Yaffle\n\n`@` becomes valuable when a downstream workspace has additional prerequisites not directly upstream of the original selected node.\n\nThis is useful for CI/preview-style targeted execution where you want:\n\n- a focal workspace\n- everything downstream that might be affected\n- all prerequisites required to make those downstream runs valid\n\n### Set operators\n\nAgain follow dbt-style rules:\n\n- space-delimited selectors = union\n- comma-delimited selectors = intersection\n- `--exclude` subtracts from the final set\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra +apps/control-plane/infra\"\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"env:main,changed+\"\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\" --exclude \"apps/docs/infra\"\n```\n\n## Selector methods\n\n### MVP methods\n\nRecommended MVP selector methods:\n\n#### `path:`\n\nMatch workspace path or glob.\n\n```bash\npath:apps/*/infra\n```\n\n#### `env:`\n\nMatch workspaces valid for an environment.\n\n```bash\nenv:main\nenv:pr-123\n```\n\n#### `changed`\n\nMatch workspaces affected by the current diff or supplied git range.\n\n```bash\nchanged\nchanged+\n```\n\nThis is one of the most compelling Yaffle-native selectors.\n\n#### `approval:`\n\nMatch workspaces that require approval in the selected environment.\n\n```bash\napproval:required\napproval:none\n```\n\nThis maps cleanly to current `approvals` config in `yaffle.toml`.\n\n### Likely phase 2 methods\n\n#### `selector:`\n\nNamed selector stored in config.\n\n```bash\nselector:frontend\nselector:foundation\n```\n\n#### `repo:`\n\nUseful once multi-repo orchestration becomes more explicit.\n\n```bash\nrepo:owner/repo\n```\n\n#### `state:`\n\nFor advanced selection from prior run artifacts or manifests.\n\n```bash\nstate:modified\nstate:failed\n```\n\n#### `tag:` or `group:`\n\nOnly if Yaffle adds first-class workspace tags/groups to config.\nThese are attractive but not required for MVP.\n\n## Recommended selector UX\n\n### Use `yaffle ls` as the safe preview primitive\n\nLike `dbt ls`, the selector language should always be previewable.\n\nThis should be the standard debugging loop:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\n### Always persist the resolved selection\n\nFor every CLI-triggered run group, store:\n\n- raw selector string\n- exclude selector string\n- resolved workspace list\n- target context (`env`, `pr`, `ref`)\n- source upload metadata\n\nThis is important for auditability and UI clarity.\n\n## UI implications\n\n### Manual CLI run groups should show up in existing environment pages\n\nBecause CLI-driven multi-workspace execution aligns with `run_group`, the current environment/PR UI can likely be reused with minimal conceptual changes.\n\nRecommended additions:\n\n- badge: `CLI`\n- initiator identity\n- original selector string\n- resolved workspace set count\n- local-upload/dirty indicator when applicable\n\n### New run group metadata to surface\n\nFor manual runs, show:\n\n- `trigger = manual`\n- `source = cli`\n- selector expression\n- exclusions\n- whether the source bundle came from current git HEAD or a local dirty upload\n\n## Queueing implications\n\n### Good news: CLI aligns with current fairness model\n\nIf CLI-triggered multi-workspace operations become `run_group`s, then the current scheduler's fairness-by-run-group model remains a good fit.\n\nThat means the queueing mismatch is less severe for Yaffle CLI than for TFC remote runs.\n\n### What still needs to change\n\nThe shared execution layer is still useful underneath:\n\n- webhook-driven run groups\n- CLI-driven manual run groups\n- TFC/OpenTofu single-workspace runs\n\nBut CLI does **not** force a full product-model rewrite of the current orchestration layer.\n\n## Relationship to TFC/OpenTofu compatibility\n\nThis framing suggests a better build order:\n\n1. strengthen Yaffle-native manual/CLI execution first\n2. build the shared execution substrate underneath it\n3. add TFC/OpenTofu compatibility on top of those primitives\n\nThat does not mean abandoning TFC compatibility.\nIt means the compatibility work should be downstream of a product-native execution story.\n\n## Recommended implementation order\n\n### Phase A: selector engine + CLI planning UX\n\n- define selector grammar\n- implement `yaffle ls`\n- implement graph resolution and preview\n- persist selector expressions on manual run groups\n\n### Phase B: manual run-group execution from CLI\n\n- support source upload from CLI\n- create `run_group(trigger = manual)` from CLI invocation\n- create deployments for the resolved workspace set\n- reuse current DAG scheduler/orchestration\n\n### Phase C: unify lower execution layer\n\n- add shared execution normalization under deployments and future TFC runs\n- standardize artifact handling\n- standardize logs/status mapping\n\n### Phase D: TFC/OpenTofu compatibility\n\n- add configuration versions\n- add runs/plans/applies\n- map TFC runs onto the shared execution substrate\n\n## MVP examples\n\n```bash\n# Show the impact set before doing anything\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n\n# Plan a workspace and everything it depends on remotely\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n\n# Plan only changed workspaces plus their downstream dependents\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n\n# Plan changed workspaces in main, excluding docs\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"env:main,changed+\" --exclude \"apps/docs/infra\"\n\n# Apply a previously reviewed manual run\nyaffle apply --from-run <run-group-or-run-id>\n```\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should `changed` compare against git merge-base, the latest successful environment run, or both depending on context?\n- Should bare selectors match exact workspace path only, or path-glob by default?\n- Should CLI uploads include dirty working tree changes in MVP, or start with committed git state only?\n- Should `apply` always require `--from-run` for named environments to reinforce reviewability?\n- Do we want named selectors in `yaffle.toml` in MVP, or later once the ```

- Common flags:

--exclude
--env <name>
--pr <number>
--wait
--json

```bash
foo          # exact workspace/path
+foo         # foo and all upstream deps
foo+         # foo and all downstream dependents
+foo+        # both directions

@foo         # foo, downstreams, and all deps needed to make those downstreams runnable
```

path:apps/*/infra
env:main
changed
approval:required

- Both should share the lower execution substrate

- should bare selectors be exact path or glob?
- should MVP allow dirty working tree uploads?
- should `apply` on named envs require `--from-run`?

dbt’s set algebra is powerful, but it’s also one of the least intuitive parts of the UX.

**My recommendation**
- keep DAG expansion
- drop generic intersection syntax
- drop inline exclude syntax
- maybe even defer generic set algebra entirely

So the MVP becomes:

```bash
yaffle ls --env main --select "apps/infra"
yaffle ls --env main --select "+apps/infra"
yaffle ls --env main --select "apps/infra+"
yaffle ls --env main --select "+apps/infra+"
```

If you need multiple roots, make union explicit at the CLI level, not inside the selector language:

```bash
yaffle plan --env main --select "+apps/infra" --select "apps/web/infra"
```

That’s much clearer than dbt’s whitespace/comma rules.

**What I’d omit in v1**
- comma intersection
- space-vs-comma meaning changes
- inline subtraction
- probably quantified graph ops too, unless you already know you need them

**What I’d keep**
- bare path selector
- `+foo`, `foo+`, `+foo+`
- maybe `changed` as a first-class special selector
- `--env` / `--pr` as top-level targeting, not selector methods if possible

**Why this is better for infra**
- fewer surprising blast-radius mistakes
- easier to explain in UI
- easier to audit later
- easier to store and replay
- better fit for “one run = one operator intent”

If you ever need more power later, I’d add it in this order:
1. multiple `--select` flags for explicit union
2. named selectors in `yaffle.toml`
3. `--exclude` as a top-level flag
4. only then consider intersections

So yes: I’d omit intersection entirely for now, and probably omit exclude too.

A good MVP rule could be:
- selector strings are only for graph expansion around roots
- composition happens via normal CLI flags, not mini-language tricks

If you want, I can update the Linear docs to this simpler selector philosophy next.

flags\n\nRecommended shared flags:\n\n- `--select`, `-s`\n- `--env <name>`\n- `--pr <number>`\n- `--ref <git-ref>` later\n- `--wait`\n- `--json`\n- `--output <fmt>` where it improves UX\n\n### Safety defaults\n\nRecommended defaults:\n\n- `plan` is allowed broadly\n- `apply` requires explicit target context (`--env` or `--pr`)\n- protected environments still require approval/policy checks\n- all CLI execution is remote by default\n- all CLI execution is audited and surfaced in UI as `source = cli`\n\n## Source material model\n\n### CLI should upload source, not assume a webhook event\n\nA strong first-party CLI should be able to run against:\n\n- current git HEAD\n- optionally uncommitted local changes\n\nThat implies a source upload model similar to TFC configuration uploads, but at **repo scope** rather than single-workspace scope.\n\n### Recommended primitive\n\nIntroduce a generalized source bundle concept later, even if the MVP stores this in existing fields first.\n\nPossible shape:\n\n- `scope = repo | workspace`\n- `origin = webhook_scan | cli_upload | tfc_upload`\n- archive key / size / checksum\n- repo metadata if available\n- head SHA if available\n- dirty flag for local uncommitted uploads\n\nPotential mapping:\n\n- webhook flow: scanner-produced repo bundle\n- CLI flow: client-uploaded repo bundle\n- TFC flow: uploaded workspace bundle\n\nThis bundle concept can unify artifact handling over time.\n\n## Selector syntax proposal\n\nTake inspiration from dbt's **graph operators**, but intentionally keep the MVP much simpler than dbt's full selector language.\n\n### Design principles\n\n- terse enough for daily use\n- graph-aware by default\n- obvious blast radius\n- easy to preview with `yaffle ls`\n- easy to store and audit\n- avoid mini-language tricks that are hard to explain in docs or UI\n\n### MVP selector philosophy\n\nThe MVP should be **graph-only**.\n\nKeep:\n\n- workspace root selection\n- upstream/downstream expansion\n- one or two built-in convenience selectors like `changed`\n\nDefer:\n\n- intersection syntax\n- subtraction / exclude syntax\n- inline set algebra\n- selector-method soup\n- complex precedence rules\n\n### Default selector\n\nA bare selector matches a workspace path.\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n### Graph operators\n\nRecommended MVP grammar:\n\n- `foo` = just this workspace\n- `+foo` = workspace and all upstream dependencies\n- `foo+` = workspace and all downstream dependents\n- `+foo+` = both upstream and downstream\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"apps/web/infra+\"\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra+\"\n```\n\n### Keep the grammar intentionally small\n\nRecommended to defer for now:\n\n- `2+foo+1`\n- `@foo`\n- `path:` prefixes\n- `env:` selector methods\n- generic unions\n- generic intersections\n- `--exclude`\n\nIf the CLI needs more power later, add it gradually after the simple model has proven itself.\n\n## Built-in selector keywords\n\n### `changed`\n\nThe strongest non-path selector for Yaffle is `changed`.\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --pr 123 --select \"changed\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n```\n\nThis gives Yaffle a high-value, product-native selector without pulling in a broad selector language.\n\n### Targeting should stay in flags, not selectors\n\nPrefer:\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\nOver:\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --select \"env:main,+apps/infra\"\n```\n\nThat keeps the selector focused on workspace/DAG intent and keeps environment context explicit.\n\n## Composition strategy\n\n### MVP: avoid generic set algebra\n\nFor the first version, keep composition simple:\n\n- one selector expression per invocation\n- one clear target context (`--env` or `--pr`)\n- one preview command (`yaffle ls`) before execution\n\nIf users later need multiple roots, add an explicit CLI-level mechanism such as repeated `--select` flags or named selectors. Do **not** start with dbt-style space/comma semantics.\n\n## Recommended selector UX\n\n### Use `yaffle ls` as the safe preview primitive\n\nLike `dbt ls`, the selector language should always be previewable.\n\nThis should be the standard debugging loop:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\n### Always persist the resolved selection\n\nFor every CLI-triggered run group, store:\n\n- raw selector string\n- resolved workspace list\n- target context (`env`, `pr`, `ref`)\n- source upload metadata\n\nThis is important for auditability and UI clarity.\n\n## UI implications\n\n### Manual CLI run groups should show up in existing environment pages\n\nBecause CLI-driven multi-workspace execution aligns with `run_group`, the current environment/PR UI can likely be reused with minimal conceptual changes.\n\nRecommended additions:\n\n- badge: `CLI`\n- initiator identity\n- original selector string\n- resolved workspace set count\n- local-upload/dirty indicator when applicable\n\n### New run group metadata to surface\n\nFor manual runs, show:\n\n- `trigger = manual`\n- `source = cli`\n- selector expression\n- whether the source bundle came from current git HEAD or a local dirty upload\n\n## Queueing implications\n\n### Good news: CLI aligns with current fairness model\n\nIf CLI-triggered multi-workspace operations become `run_group`s, then the current scheduler's fairness-by-run-group model remains a good fit.\n\nThat means the queueing mismatch is less severe for Yaffle CLI than for TFC remote runs.\n\n### What still needs to change\n\nThe shared execution layer is still useful underneath:\n\n- webhook-driven run groups\n- CLI-driven manual run groups\n- TFC/OpenTofu single-workspace runs\n\nBut CLI does **not** force a full product-model rewrite of the current orchestration layer.\n\n## Relationship to TFC/OpenTofu compatibility\n\nThis framing suggests a better build order:\n\n1. strengthen Yaffle-native manual/CLI execution first\n2. build the shared execution substrate underneath it\n3. add TFC/OpenTofu compatibility on top of those primitives\n\nThat does not mean abandoning TFC compatibility.\nIt means the compatibility work should be downstream of a product-native execution story.\n\n## Recommended implementation order\n\n### Phase A: selector engine + CLI planning UX\n\n- define selector grammar\n- implement `yaffle ls`\n- implement graph resolution and preview\n- persist selector expressions on manual run groups\n\n### Phase B: manual run-group execution from CLI\n\n- support source upload from CLI\n- create `run_group(trigger = manual)` from CLI invocation\n- create deployments for the resolved workspace set\n- reuse current DAG scheduler/orchestration\n\n### Phase C: unify lower execution layer\n\n- add shared execution normalization under deployments and future TFC runs\n- standardize artifact handling\n- standardize logs/status mapping\n\n### Phase D: TFC/OpenTofu compatibility\n\n- add configuration versions\n- add runs/plans/applies\n- map TFC runs onto the shared execution substrate\n\n## MVP examples\n\n```bash\n# Show the impact set before doing anything\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n\n# Plan a workspace and everything it depends on remotely\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n\n# Plan only changed workspaces plus their downstream dependents\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n\n# Apply a previously reviewed manual run\nyaffle apply --from-run <run-group-or-run-id>\n```\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should `changed` compare against git merge-base, the latest successful environment run, or both depending on context?\n- Should CLI uploads include dirty working tree changes in MVP, or start with committed git state only?\n- Should `apply` always require `--from-run` for named environments to reinforce reviewability?\n- When we eventually need multiple roots, should that be repeated `--select` flags, named selectors, or both?"

workspace metadata\n\n### Phase D: UI and eventing\n\n- keep environment/DAG pages for webhook + CLI run groups\n- add workspace-run pages for compatibility flows\n- add generic execution/workspace-run event families where needed\n\n### Phase E: compatibility validation and polish\n\n- validate with real `tofu init`, `tofu plan`, and `tofu apply`\n- confirm no local AWS credentials are needed\n- add saved-plan support and richer actions later if still justified\n\n## Non-negotiables\n\n- do not couple this work to the legacy local runner\n- do not conflate cloud backend execution mode with internal runner kind\n- preserve tenant isolation at every workspace/configuration-version/run/state boundary\n- fail closed on missing workspace ownership, missing token scope, or ambiguous auth context\n- keep Yaffle-managed webhook DAG execution working while adding TFC remote execution\n\n## Suggested next step\n\nStart with **Phase A + Phase B** first:\n\n- lock the simple CLI selector grammar\n- define how a manual CLI invocation becomes a `run_group`\n- add the shared execution abstraction\n- make scheduler fairness operate on normalized queue groups\n\nOnce that lands, the TFC/OpenTofu route layer becomes much more mechanical."

{"id":"74f75714-dd29-4c71-b26f-1c7c039fd346","title":"Yaffle CLI DAG selector draft","content":"## Why this matters\n\nThe remote execution investment becomes much more compelling when the primary surface is the first-party `yaffle` CLI rather than only TFC/OpenTofu compatibility.\n\nThis reframes the work as:\n\n* **primary**: Yaffle-native remote execution for operators and developers\n* than asking users to think in terms of raw TFC backend semantics.\n\n## Product stance\n\n### Recommended positioning\n\n* Yaffle remains a **PR-first**, preview-first infrastructure delivery **multiple workspaces**\n* they should respect the **workspace DAG**\n* they should show up in the **same environment-oriented UI**\n* they should reuse **run-group fairness and orchestration**\n\nThat means a Yaffle CLI invocation likely maps naturally to:\n\n* `run_group` with `trigger = \"manual\"`\n* `workspace_deployments` for the selected workspaces\n* normalized `yaffle ls`\n\nPreview which workspaces a selector resolves to.\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle ls --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n```\n\n#### `yaffle graph`\n\nShow workspaces.\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n#### `yaffle apply`\n\nApply a previously reviewed plan or trigger run.\n\n```bash\nyaffle logs run_123\nyaffle logs deploy_123\n```\n\n### Common targeting flags\n\nRecommended shared flags:\n\n* `--select`, `-s`\n* `--env <name>`\n* `--pr <number>`\n* `--ref <git-ref>` later\n* `--wait`\n* `--json`\n* `--output <fmt>` where it improves UX\n\n### Safety defaults\n\nRecommended defaults:\n\n* `plan` is allowed broadly\n* `apply` requires explicit target context (`--env` or `--pr`)\n* protected environments still require approval/policy checks\n* all CLI execution is remote by default\n* all CLI execution is audited and surfaced in UI as `source = graph-aware by default\n* obvious blast radius\n* easy to preview with `yaffle ls`\n* easy to store and audit\n* avoid mini-language tricks that are hard to explain in docs or UI\n\n### MVP selector philosophy\n\nThe MVP should be **graph-only**.\n\nKeep:\n\n* workspace root selection\n* upstream/downstream expansion\n* one or two built-in convenience selectors like `changed`\n\nDefer:\n\n* intersection syntax\n* subtraction / exclude syntax\n* inline set algebra\n* selector-method soup\n* complex precedence rules\n\n### Default selector\n\nA bare selector matches a workspace path.\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\n```\n\n### Graph operators\n\nRecommended MVP grammar:\n\n* `foo` = just this workspace\n* `+foo` = workspace and all upstream dependencies\n* `foo+` = workspace and all downstream dependents\n* `+foo+` = both upstream and downstream\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"apps/web/infra\"\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"apps/web/infra+\"\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra+\"\n```\n\n### Keep the grammar intentionally small\n\nRecommended to defer for now:\n\n* `2+foo+1`\n\n`If t`he C`LI ne`eds more powe`r la`ter, add it gradually after the simple model has proven itself.\n\n## `Built-in` selector keywords\n\n### changed\n\nThe strongest non-path selector for Yaffle is changed.\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --pr 123 --select \"changed\"\nyaffle plan --pr 123 --select \"changed+\"\n```\n\nThis g`ives Ya`ffle a high-value, product-native selector without pulling in a broad selector language.\n\n### Targeting should stay in flags, not selectors\n\nPrefer:\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\nOver:\n\n```bash\nyaffle plan --select \"env:main,+apps/infra\"\n```\n\nThat keeps the selector focused on workspace/DAG intent and keeps environment context explicit.\n\n## Composition strategy\n\n### MVP: avoid generic set algebra\n\nFor the first version, keep composition simple:\n\n* one selector expression per invocation\n\nIf users later need multiple roots, add an explicit CLI-level mechanism such as repeated --`select` flags or named selectors. Do not st`art w`ith `dbt-`style space/comma semantic`s.`\n\n## `Recom`mended selector UX\n\n### Use `yaffle ls` as the safe preview primitive\n\nLike `dbt ls`, the selector language should alwa`ys` be previewable.\n\nThis should be the **st**andard debugging loop:\n\n```bash\nyaffle ls --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle graph --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\nyaffle plan --env main --select \"+apps/infra\"\n```\n\n### Always persist the resolved selection\n\nFor every CLI-triggered run group, store:\n\n* raw selector string\n* resolved workspace list\n* target context (`env`, `pr`, `ref`)\n* source upload metadata\n\nThis is important for auditability and UI clarity.\n\n## UI implications\n\n### Manual CLI run groups should show up in existing environment pages\n\nBecause CLI-driven multi-workspace execution aligns with `run_group`, the current environment/PR UI can likely be reused with minimal conceptual changes.\n\nRecommended additions:\n\n* badge: `CLI`\n* initiator identity\n* original selector string\n* resolved workspace set count\n* local-upload/dirty indicator when applicable\n\n### New run group metadata to surface\n\nFor manual runs, show:\n\n* `trigger = manual`\n* `source = cli`\n* selector expression\n* whether the source bundle came from current git HEAD or a local dirty upload\n\n## Queueing implications\n\n### Good news: CLI aligns with current fairness model\n\nIf CLI-triggered multi-workspace operations become `run_group`s, then the current scheduler's fairness-by-run-group model remains a good fit.\n\nThat means the queueing CLI-driven manual run groups\n* TFC/OpenTofu single-workspace runs\n\nBut CLI does **not** force a full product-model rewrite of the current orchestration layer.\n\n## Relationship to TFC/OpenTofu compatibility\n\nThis framing suggests a better build order:\n\n1. strengthen Yaffle-native manual/CLI execution first\n2. build the shared execution substrate underneath it\n3. add TFC/OpenTofu compatibility on top of those primitives\n\nThat does not mean abandoning TFC compatibility.\nIt means the compatibility work should be downstream of a product-native execution story.\n\n## Workspace API still advertises local execution\n\nThe TFC workspace response currently hardcodes:\n\n* `execution-mode = \"local\"`\n* org `default-execution-mode = \"local\"`\n\n**That is correct** **fo**r **the cu**rrent state-hosting implementation, but it is incompatible with real remote execution.\n\n### 2\\. Yaffle's execution core is deployment-centric, not workspace-run-centric\n\nCurrent execution tables and routes are optimized for webhook-driven Yaffle deployments:\n\n* `workspace_deployments`\n* `tf_runs` with required `deployment_id`\n* `iac_jobs` with required `deployment_id`\n* runner completion paths that recover workspace identity from deployment metadata\n\nThis is a mismatch for TFC/OpenTofu remote runs, because a CLI/API-triggered run can exist **outside** a webhook-created deployment/run-group.\n\nThis is the biggest structural incompatibility.\n\n### 3\\. Token scopes are state/workspace oriented, not run oriented\n\nUser tokens currently cover workspace/state operations and force unlock, but do not yet express:\n\n* queue run\n* apply run\n* cancel run\n* discard run\n* plan JSON access if needed\n\n### 6\\. Yep — I updated the plan to keep the selector story simple.

- `YAF-160`: https://linear.app/yaffledev/issue/YAF-160/execute-opentofu-remote-execution-plan
- `OpenTofu remote execution plan`: https://linear.app/yaffledev/document/opentofu-remote-execution-plan-20120b6d64eb
- `Yaffle CLI DAG selector draft`: https://linear.app/yaffledev/document/yaffle-cli-dag-selector-draft-bb134954e179

What we’re standardizing on for MVP:

- keep only graph-aware selectors:
  - `foo`
  - `+foo`
  - `foo+`
  - `+foo+`
  - `changed`
- keep targeting out of the selector language:
  - `--env main`
  - `--pr 123`
- omit for now:
  - union/intersection syntax
  - `--exclude`
  - comma/space precedence rules
  - quantified graph operators like `2+foo+1`
  - method-heavy syntax like `env:main,path:...`

So the happy path becomes:

```bash
yaffle ls --env main --select "+apps/infra"
yaffle graph --env main --select "+apps/infra"
yaffle plan --env main --select "+apps/infra"
yaffle plan --pr 123 --select "changed+"
yaffle apply --from-run rg_123
```

I think this is the right call because it keeps:
- blast radius obvious
- audit trails readable
- UI explanations straightforward
- room to add repeated `--select` or named selectors later if we actually need composition

Next best step is to lock the exact selector grammar and semantics for `changed`, then design `yaffle ls` around that.

browser to terminal and feel like they are in the same product.\n\n### Avoid terminal-only renaming\n\nDo not rename core concepts in the TUI just because it is a terminal surface.\n\nKeep:\n\n- environment\n- run group\n- workspace\n- plan\n- apply\n- approval\n\nConsistent naming will matter a lot.\n\n## Suggested implementation order\n\n### Phase 1: TUI shell and browsing\n\n- add `yaffle` flows\n\n- support `yaffle plan --env main` opening selection TUI\n- support selector input in TUI or CLI flag\n- show resolved DAG and workspace set before dispatch\n\n### Phase 3: attached run questions\n\n- Should `yaffle plan --env main` always open the TUI if no selector is given, or only when stdout is a TTY?\n- Should `yaffle apply --from-run <id>` auto-attach to the TUI after
